suite.name: Bandwidth

kw.name: Open Bench
kw.doc: Load the bench, its calibration and the radio file, and prepare the instruments. All four are mandatory and differ from tester to tester, so suites take them from the command line (-v BENCH:... and so on). `firmware` names what the radio runs, such as a git describe.

test.name: FM TX At 25 kHz Stays Within Wide Limits

kw.name: Create Audio Tone
kw.doc: Write a tone WAV for the operator to play into the radio's mic.

kw.name: Operator Does
kw.arg: Set the radio to FM, 445.975 MHz, 25 kHz bandwidth, low power, programming cable out
kw.doc: Ask the operator to do something and wait until it's done.

kw.name: Capture Radio Transmissions
kw.msg:
capture01
peak dev Hzrms dev Hztone HzOBW 99% Hzoffset Hzsaudio
tx177438910004000736959
tx247752814164113000736986
kw.arg: Play ${tone} at a fixed volume and distance from the mic, key PTT for 5 s, release. Then key PTT, whistle loudly close to the mic for 5 s, release.
kw.doc: Record while the operator follows the instruction, then measure each FM transmission. Fails unless exactly `expected` are found. Returns the measurements, oldest first; each one's audio is saved as a WAV.

kw.name: Fm Transmission Should Meet Limits
kw.doc: Check peak deviation and occupied bandwidth against the radio file's limits for a channel bandwidth (BW_12_5 or BW_25).

suite.doc:
FM follows the 12.5/25 kHz channel bandwidth setting, on transmit and on receive.
Transmit is measured from the SDR capture. Receive is judged by the operator, until the radio can report its own audio. The programming cable stays out throughout: it disconnects the mic and the speaker.
To measure stock firmware as a reference, run with --exclude m17 and compare the two exports with oat compare.
